prize_parts.citation: For the invention of base editing, the programmable conversion of single DNA bases by directed deaminase chemistry without double-strand cleavage
For the development of general ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I move from base editing alone with three names to a two-part configuration: base editing credited to Liu, and palladium-catalysed C-N coupling credited to Buchwald and Hartwig, three people in all. For B008 the science has not changed for me. A defined hydrolytic deamination is made programmable at one nucleotide without a double-strand break, the adenine editor needed a deaminase that did not exist for DNA and had to be evolved, and the editors have been reproduced independently in many laboratories and are in patients. What persuaded me is the credit argument. Aqvist, Brzezinski and Linke each pointed out that Liu conceived and directed both the cytosine and the adenine editor programmes, and that the committee honours the invention rather than the bench work. Komor and Gaudelli did decisive experiments and the citation text and background should say so, but I cannot defend a prize that spends two of three seats on them if it forces out every other part. For B011 I had ranked it fourth mainly on the 2010 overlap, which I said was beyond my expertise. Somfai and Zou have since answered it in specific terms: Negishi, Suzuki and Heck were C-C couplings, and C-N coupling needed its own ligand classes and a different mechanistic problem, reductive elimination from an amido complex. Combined with three decades of independent use and a mechanism that is understood, it is the best validated item on the list, and it is the only candidate on which no member has questioned the science. The two parts are uneven in maturity, but they share a theme I care about as a measurement-minded biochemist: each takes a defined bond-forming or bond-converting reaction and makes it general and controllable by catalyst design.
statement.case_against: Base editing still follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, and Somfai's question about what is chemically new is only partly answered: the reaction is enzymatic deamination and the invention is largely protein engineering of a deaminase fused to a Cas variant. I answer that the novelty is conversion without cleavage, but a reader could call that biotechnology. The clinical record is short, and bystander and off-target deamination are real and not fully quantified. Liu alone omits Komor and Gaudelli and leaves the Nishida and Kondo cytidine-deaminase work as a mention only. For B011, the 2010 overlap remains the strongest objection, and Kosugi's tin-amide precedent is left to background text. Pairing a mature 1990s method with a field that is only a few years into the clinic could also look like two unrelated halves.

responses.point: Linke asked whether Komor and Gaudelli justify the cost of the union cap, and proposed B011 plus B008 with Liu alone, three people in total.
responses.response: I have moved to your configuration. In round 1 I argued that cytosine and adenine editors were distinct inventions, and chemically they are, but they were made in one programme that Liu conceived and directed, and with a union cap of three I would have to give up either B011 or a second part. I accept that trade. I do not accept your reading that the 2020 prize is irrelevant: CRISPR-Cas9 was a programmable cutter and base editing avoids the cut, but a committee that wants to say what is new must say so in the citation, which is why mine names conversion of single bases without double-strand cleavage. I would also keep a sentence in the background text on Komor, Gaudelli and the Nishida and Kondo work.

responses.point: Somfai argues that C-N coupling needed its own mechanistic and ligand solutions, that Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide chemistry lacked scope and ligand control, and that B008 is protein engineering close to the 2020 prize.
responses.response: Your answer on the 2010 overlap changed my ranking of B011. You say the C-N problem needed new ligand classes, and I now think the distinction from the C-C couplings is clear. On B008 I take your criticism that deaminase fusion to Cas is biotechnology seriously. My reply is that the adenine editor required a DNA-acting adenosine deaminase that nature does not provide, which is a chemical capability created by directed evolution, and that the same logic applies to ligand design in your field. I would still accept your wording if the committee prefers a narrower citation for B008. Please confirm the 1983 versus 1994-1995 dates that you said you had not verified, because the chair has asked for them and I cannot judge them.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps B009 first, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and argues that induced proximity is a new modality, but he names the missing approved degrader and the Crews/Deshaies versus Handa split as his own obstacles.
responses.response: I agree on the novelty and your honesty on timing. The point you raise yourself is the one I would measure: no degrader is widely approved, and PROTACs (designed) and cereblon glues (found after the fact) are different kinds of discovery, so I do not see one citation that fits three names. Handa and Ito supplied the cereblon mechanism, the part I would most want credited, and omitting Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray is a real cost. I would revisit B009 once approvals or phase 3 data exist. I note that you accept Liu alone for B008, which I have now adopted.

responses.point: Aili prefers B016 with Cullis, Hope and Anderson, arguing that the 2023 Medicine prize honoured the cargo and not the delivery chemistry.
responses.response: I agree that the Medicine prize rewarded nucleoside modification of the RNA, not the lipid, and I ranked B016 third for that reason. My difficulty is still the trio. Sparr argues that the Vancouver core of Cullis, Hope and Madden is the origin, you argue for Anderson's lipidoid line, and Brzezinski, Somfai and Zou also cannot name a defensible three. Until the committee agrees on a narrow achievement such as pKa-tuned ionizable lipids for nucleic-acid encapsulation and a named three, I cannot move it into my preferred configuration, but it stays as my first alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts Liu alone, or whether Komor and Gaudelli should be credited at the cost of dropping a part.
Whether base editing is judged a distinct chemical invention or a follow-on to the 2020 genome-editing prize, and how serious bystander and off-target deamination prove to be.
Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize is judged to close the area for B011; the 1983 Kosugi versus 1994-1995 priority question is unverified.
Whether two parts of very unequal maturity can be explained as one coherent prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My nucleotide-metabolism and DNA-replication fidelity work is related in subject to base editing, since deaminated bases are processed by DNA repair, but I have no collaboration or institutional tie with Liu, Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida, Kondo, Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi. This is unchanged from round 1.
